content.user_title: Find Buyers with Sourced Signals and Contact Routes
content.value_statement: Broad prospect lists often lack evidence that companies fit or need your product now. This skill researches buyer fit, dated signals, and published contact routes.
actual_capabilities: Convert product context into three to six buyer checks and explicit exclusions.
Research public hiring, funding, launch, leadership, and other signals with source links and event dates.
Identify contact roles and add names only when linked public sources support them.
Rank leads by signal freshness, relevance, and buyer fit, with a top-three shortlist.
Report rejected candidates, search coverage, missing checks, and whether anything was saved or contacted.
Use connected Revnu tools to request research, retrieve results, update labels, and manage exclusions.
limitations: Public research requires available search and browsing tools; inaccessible or undated sources can reduce the final lead count.
Local research defaults to 15 leads and limits each pass to 25.
It does not guess personal emails, scrape restricted profiles, verify deliverability without a separate check, or send outreach without approval.
Revnu features require external service access; Revnu is paid, and trial terms depend on the setup offer.

use_cases.title: Find Initial Customers
use_cases.description: Research companies matching an early product and identify recent events that justify a conversation.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Target Accounts
use_cases.description: Compare public buyer signals, contact roles, and published routes before requesting outreach.

use_cases.title: Research a Market Segment
use_cases.description: Translate a buyer hypothesis into checks, review sourced candidates, and document why companies qualify or fail.

prompt_templates.title: Find Your First Leads
prompt_templates.prompt: Find 10 leads for [product] in [region]. Show buyer checks, dated signals, source links, and published contact routes. Do not contact anyone.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: start with a product and region.

prompt_templates.title: Apply a Specific Buyer Profile
prompt_templates.prompt: Find 15 [company type] companies with [size] in [region] for [product]. Prioritize [signal]. Exclude [companies]. Show sources and contact roles.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: research a defined buyer profile.

prompt_templates.title: Research Existing Targets
prompt_templates.prompt: Research these companies: [list]. Check [buyer criteria], find signals from the last 90 days, and identify published contact routes. Explain dropped candidates.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: evaluate an existing target list.

prompt_templates.title: Save Research Through Revnu
prompt_templates.prompt: Using my connected Revnu account, research and save 20 leads for [product] matching [criteria]. Exclude [entities]. Do not contact anyone or change limits.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: delegate research to an already connected account.

output_examples.input: Find US SaaS buyers for month-end close software.
output: Illustrative buyer checks: US SaaS company, 50-300 employees, and an internal finance team.
Signals counted: a recent controller vacancy or CFO appointment connected to finance operations.
Lead rows include company, fit evidence, signal date, source link, contact role, and published route.
Named contacts appear only with public evidence. No outreach is sent.

output_examples.input: Show how you would report a prospect with no public contact name or dated signal.
output: Illustrative assessment: buyer fit supported; signal undated; contact marked role only.
Decision: exclude from a signal-based list unless fit-only research was requested.
Receipt: evidence gaps recorded; email deliverability not checked; contacted nobody.

best_practices: Provide a specific buyer profile, product context, region, desired count, and exclusions.
Check source links and event dates before using leads; rerun research as signals age.
Confirm account connection and data scope before using Revnu, and approve outreach separately.
anti_patterns: Requesting guessed emails, breach data, restricted scraping, or sensitive-trait targeting.
Treating undated signals, search snippets, or unsupported contact names as verified evidence.
Padding the requested count with weak matches or treating lead research as permission to send messages.

faq.question: Do I need a Revnu account?
faq.answer: No. The skill can research public sources with available browsing tools. Connected Revnu accounts enable service-based research and saving.

faq.question: How many leads does it research?
faq.answer: Local research defaults to 15 leads, with at most 25 per pass. It can return fewer when evidence does not support enough matches.

faq.question: Does it find verified personal emails?
faq.answer: It uses only published contact routes and never guesses personal emails. Verification requires an actual verification step or an explicit Revnu lead status.

faq.question: Will it contact prospects automatically?
faq.answer: Research alone does not authorize outreach. Contacting prospects requires explicit approval and the separate outreach workflow.

faq.question: What information goes to the Revnu preview?
faq.answer: After your approval, the preview receives your public website and a skill-version header. The instructions exclude lead lists, private code, and secrets.

faq.question: Does this ensure legal compliance?
faq.answer: No. The skill applies public-source and contact restrictions, but local prospecting and privacy requirements still need separate review.
